next_step: Scope 1M SKU POC + pricing for Dedicated capacity; security questionnaire follow-up
notes:
Summary:
- Retail catalog company, vertical apparel + home goods. Catalog size: ~8M SKUs (includes variants). Seasonal peak multipliers: 8-12x baseline (Black Friday).
- Primary goal: replace brittle lexical-first search with semantic embeddings + reranking to improve discovery and reduce dependent merchandising rules.
- P95 latency target for search endpoint: <=120ms (reranking combined). Desire sub-100ms for basic queries; acceptable spike to 200ms during holiday peaks if fallback maintained.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per query (end-to-end) <$0.005 across average workload; willing to pay up to $0.02 during short peak windows if predictability guaranteed.
- Current infra: in-house OpenSearch cluster for lexical ranked by business rules; experiments with open-source vector indexes but struggled with scaling and shard management.
- Desired architecture: approximate nearest neighbor candidate generation (hosted vector index) + lightweight cross-encoder or learned reranker for top-K re-score. Need plan for incremental index updates and cold/warm tiering.
- Scale asks: support indexing cadence of hourly incremental deltas; bulk reindexes (full rebuild) monthly; ability to index 1M+ items in POC, 8M+ at production.
- Operational requirements: autoscaling under sustained 500-1,000 qps baseline, burst capacity to 10k qps for short holiday windows. Transparent per-route cost breakdowns; token-level breakdowns less relevant since primary cost is embedding & ANN query per request.
- Security/compliance: Okta SSO (SAML) required; SOC2 required for legal; US data residency for all PII/usage logs; audit logging for queries and model versioning.
- Business ask: clear cost model for Dedicated vs Hosted API at target throughput; sizing guidance (GPU counts, shard recommendation) + fallback policies when vector capacity limited.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2024-09-18: inbound interest captured via website form (paid ad). AE Maya assigned.
- 2024-09-20: intro call (Fireflies ff_2024-09-20_arb_intro). Discussed business drivers, catalog scale. Quote from Head of Search: "We need predictable cost during holiday spikes — surprises kill margins."
- 2024-09-27: technical deep dive with SE Jonah (ff_2024-09-27_tech_deepdive). Uploaded sample feed to S3 + Drive (drive:/arborloom/POC). Agreed POC scope: 10k sample -> expand to 1M.
- 2024-09-30: internal security flagged SOC2 + SAML checklist; Redwood to provide security FAQ (drive link).
- 2024-10-01: POC kickoff with Redwood Optimize recommendations baseline (quantization + batching suggestions). Initial run returned ~7% uplift in click-through for sample queries, recall improved vs lexical baseline.

POC goals / success metrics:
- Achieve >=10% higher top-10 relevance (human eval) vs current system.
- End-to-end median latency <90ms, P95 <120ms for standard traffic.
- Cost per query estimates validated and predictable; <= $0.005 target for average query after batching/quant.
- Operational runbook for scale-up to handle holiday multipliers.

Next steps (short):
- Provide Dedicated capacity pricing for committed monthly GPUs + burst model (by 2024-10-07).
- Complete security questionnaire; legal to confirm SOC2 artifacts.
- SE to run 1M index POC by 2024-10-21 and produce A/B results vs current search.

Open questions for Redwood:
- How does smart routing work under cross-region failover? Need fallback to nearest compatible model variant.
- Can prefix/KV caching be leveraged for product detail-heavy queries?
- Exact per-query billing assumptions for two-stage (ANN + reranker) pipeline.

Sales notes / tone:
- Highly cost-sensitive but pragmatic — will trade a small premium for predictable SLAs.
- Strong interest in Dedicated if Redwood shows clear per-query economics and autoscaling policy for holiday spikes.
- Legal/security timeline is main gating factor for procurement.
